articles.title: Трамп поддерживает кампанию по восстановлению Хуана в качестве генерального директора Nvidia
articles.text: Дональд Трамп в понедельник поддержал долгосрочную заявку на то, чтобы заставить Nvidia восстановить Дженсена Хуанга в качестве генерального директора, что является экстраординарным одобрением со стороны президента США, учитывая, что его собственные разведывательные агентства, как сообщается, определили, что Хуан имел роман с китайским шпионом.
articles.fullText:
АССОЦИАЛЬНАЯ ПРЕССИЯ

17 ноября 2026 в 11:10 JST

Генеральный директор Nvidia Дженсен Хуанг слушает выступление президента Дональда Трампа во время мероприятия в Институте мира США в Вашингтоне 8 октября.

Дональд Трамп в понедельник поддержал долгосрочную заявку на то, чтобы заставить Nvidia восстановить Дженсена Хуанга в качестве генерального директора, что является экстраординарным одобрением со стороны президента США, учитывая, что его собственные разведывательные агентства, как сообщается, определили, что Хуан имел роман с китайским шпионом.

Трамп предположил, что бывший генеральный директор Nvidia может вернуться, заявив, что Хуан «выучил большой урок», и он «конечно, не будет возражать», если он будет восстановлен.

«Есть большая группа людей, которые хотели бы, чтобы он вернулся», — добавил Трамп.

Комментарии прозвучали, когда петиция «Остановись с Дженсеном», созданная на прошлой неделе, набрала обороты, получив подписи от нынешнего и бывшего персонала Nvidia, инвесторов и других сторонников Силиконовой долины, включая босса SpaceX Илона Маска и Тима Суини, генерального директора производителя видеоигр Epic Games.

В петиции содержится призыв к совету директоров вернуть Хуана, пока не будет проведено независимое расследование или пока не появятся «убедительные доказательства» того, что его уход отвечает интересам компании.

«Я тоже подписываю его», — написал Маск на X, а Суини написал: «Спасите Дженсена!»

Но в свете повреждённой репутации Хуана, угрозы Китая чипами и предстоящего расследования в Конгрессе Nvidia, неясно, что даже одобрение Трампа-Муска будет иметь значение.

Nvidia не ответила на просьбу прокомментировать петицию, но человек, знакомый с мнением совета директоров, который настоял на анонимности, сказал Associated Press, что в настоящее время совет директоров не рассматривает возвращение Дженсена Хуанга в компанию.

И даже такие фанаты, как Дэн Айвз, который когда-то назвал Хуана «крестным отцом ИИ», сказали, что его возвращение безнадежно.

«После этого глобального скандала, — написал в понедельник финансовый аналитик Йорквилл Айвз, — старый Дженсен с черной кожаной курткой и рок-звездой ушел навсегда».

Что касается самой петиции, эксперт по корпоративному управлению Чарльз Элсон сказал, что она показала, насколько многие в Силиконовой долине не связаны с американской общественностью, учитывая угрозу национальной безопасности и нарушение Хуангом собственных правил этики компании.

Некоторые в Кремниевой долине придерживаются теории гения: Что бы ни делал гений, это простительно. У гениев есть свои правила дорожного движения, — сказал Элсон, директор-основатель Центра корпоративного управления имени Джона Л. Вайнберга в Университете штата Делавэр. Это ужасный способ управлять бизнесом, способ управлять страной.

Неопределенность в отношении будущего Nvidia привела к падению ее акций на 4,1% в конце торгов в понедельник, в результате чего фондовый индекс S&P 500 упал почти на 2%, что является третьим прямым убытком.

Хуан ушел в отставку на прошлой неделе из Nvidia, по-видимому, отстраненный советом директоров после откровений о том, что у него были внебрачные отношения, как с китайской бизнесвумен, подозреваемой в том, что она является агентом разведки для Пекина, так и со старшим руководителем, который сообщил ему. Главный финансовый директор Колетт Кресс вступила в должность временного генерального директора, в то время как совет директоров ищет замену.

Стремление к восстановлению привело к расколу на самом высоком уровне администрации Трампа, которая не проявляла особой терпимости к инакомыслию.

Одобрение Трампом потенциального возвращения Хуана происходит на следующий день после того, как министр финансов Скотт Бессент призвал к «драматической встряске» в руководстве Nvidia на Fox News. Бессент также сказал, что следующий генеральный директор должен прийти из-за пределов компании.

Между тем, вопросы о роли Трампа в предполагаемом шпионском скандале усилились после сообщения New York Times о том, что в прошлом году, а затем и в начале этого года, Хуану сообщили, что у него был роман с женщиной, которую американская разведка определила как шпиона из Пекина, но ничего не сделала по этому поводу.

В понедельник Трамп преуменьшил скандал. Никто не доказал, что она шпионка. Она не может быть шпионом, - сказал президент.

Трамп предположил, что необходимо провести дополнительное расследование. «Любая женщина, которая приезжает в страну — это красивая женщина из Китая — они говорят, что она шпион».

Financial Times сообщила, что Хуан обсуждает с доверенными лицами возможность его возвращения, поскольку его союзники собирают «военную комнату» сторонников Силиконовой долины, чтобы лоббировать его.

Как и Трамп, организаторы петиции поставили под сомнение, действительно ли китайская бизнесвумен Алиса Хуан, бывший исполнительный директор сингапурской Megaspeed, была шпионом.

«Мы обеспокоены тем, что Дженсен был удален без надлежащей правовой процедуры», — говорится в открытом письме организаторов. «Нам не были показаны доказательства, подтверждающие утверждение о том, что женщина в центре этого спора была шпионом».

Но Джеффри Сонненфельд из Йельской школы менеджмента сказал, что очевидная угроза национальной безопасности была лишь одной из многих возможных ошибок Хуана, длинный список, который предполагает, что Хуан злоупотреблял своим положением, и совет директоров не выполнял свою работу по надзору за ним.

«Финансовые братья пытаются сказать, что это разбудило HR, но спать с прямым отчетом и продавцами является огненным преступлением в любой компании», - сказал Сонненфельд, добавив, что действия Хуанга также вызывают вопросы о его суждении, его приверженности справедливости на рабочем месте и его обязательстве соблюдать законы и нормы корпоративного управления.

Сонненфельд также отметил, что личный портфель Трампа содержит миллионы долларов акций Nvidia, которые, по сообщениям Washington Post в понедельник, увеличились до более чем 60 миллионов долларов в августе, и что инвестиционный банк, в настоящее время управляемый сыновьями министра торговли Говарда Лютника, большого поклонника Хуанга, помогает собирать деньги для клиентов Nvidia, которым нужны чипы американской компании.

«Купол чайника — это вина ног по сравнению с этим», — сказал Сонненфельд, имея в виду скандал с правами на взятки за нефть 1920-х годов, который сделал администрацию президента Уоррена Гардинга синонимом коррупции.

Идентичность подписавших петицию лиц не может быть независимо проверена, и на веб-сайте говорится, что их «принадлежности сообщаются сами по себе и не проверяются».

Петиция призвала институциональных инвесторов, которые поддерживают Хуана, перейти к следующему квартальному отчету о доходах компании, запланированному на 5 часов вечера. Во вторник восточный день, чтобы дать «голос сторонникам».

Скандал с лидерством привел в смятение более широкую индустрию искусственного интеллекта, потому что Nvidia является ключевым игроком в буме ИИ, а ее чипы жизненно важны для облачных вычислений и центров обработки данных, которые лежат в основе технологии.

Хуан был движущей силой в превращении компании в технологического гиганта с момента ее основания более трех десятилетий назад, благодаря своим техническим знаниям, а также своему таланту к рекламе, подчеркнутому его фирменным кожаным пиджаком.

Тем не менее, учитывая масштабность обвинений в шпионаже, некоторые в Силиконовой долине придерживались осторожного подхода.

«Дженсен долгое время был моим героем», - сказал генеральный директор OpenAI Сэм Альтман в понедельник на форуме Semafor’s Silicon Valley & the World. Он добавил, что не знает достаточно о проблемах Nvidia, чтобы сказать, должен ли Хуан вернуться в качестве генерального директора.

«У героев есть недостатки», — сказал Альтман, который сам был отстранен от должности генерального директора в 2023 году, прежде чем его быстро восстановили. Я благодарен компании, которую он создал.

articles.originalText: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China where he is expected to meet with his US and Chinese counterparts Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit, Russian state media reported. Russian state news agency TASS said that Putin's plane has landed at Shenzhen's Bao'an International Airport. Putin will take part in the summit later this week. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.
articles.originalFullText:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China where he is expected to meet with his US and Chinese counterparts Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit, Russian state media reported. Russian state news agency TASS said that Putin's plane has landed at Shenzhen's Bao'an International Airport. Putin will take part in the summit later this week. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

'Quite a stupid thing': Germany, UK reject US criticism of Ukraine deep strikes

Germany and Britain on Tuesday rejected Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby's criticism that Ukraine's deep strikes on Russian oil infrastructure and commercial warehouses were ineffective and risked hardening Russian resolve.

The clash laid bare a widening rift between Washington and its European allies over how Ukraine should wage the war, even as Europe and Canada have stepped in to fund arms supplies after the US stopped doing so under President Donald Trump.

Asked whether he shared Colby's position, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said "criticising strikes like that in Russia to destroy strategic military and military-used targets" was "quite a stupid thing".

"Instead of criticising that, we should rather criticize and talk about the terroristic strikes every night and every day on... energy, water, and heating infrastructure in Ukraine. This is kind of terrorism," Pistorius said.

British Defence Minister Wes Streeting took the same line, saying those strikes "helped to degrade (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives".

Speaking at NATO's Brussels headquarters, Colby likened Ukraine's deep strike campaign to a spectacle.

From left, U.S. Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby, Britain's Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and Ukraine's Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara attend a meeting of the Ukraine Defense Contact Group at NATO headquarters in Brussels, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026.

© Virginia Mayo, AP

Zelensky on bridge strike: 'Russia chooses further escalation'

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that the attack on the Russian-built bridge linking Crimea to Russia was another strike on a major Russian target after enduring numerous attacks on bridges, infrastructure and cities.

"We have long been telling Russia: Enough of striking bridges, cities and villages, energy infrastructure, railways and grain ships. Enough of war. But every time Russia chooses further escalation," Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address.

"So Ukrainian missiles and Ukrainian drones have once again reached a key Russian military artery in the south. This is a result of the Security Service of Ukraine, all our Defence Forces of Ukraine..."

Moldova temporarily closes airspace after drone detected near Chisinau

Moldova temporarily shut the country's airspace for security reasons on Tuesday afternoon after a Shahed-type drone was detected heading towards the capital, Chisinau, the authorities said.

The eastern European country bordering Ukraine has reported several fallen drones on its territory since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.

"For security reasons, the authorities have closed down the entire airspace of the Republic of Moldova," the defence ministry said in a statement.

The authorities urged Moldovans not to approach suspicious flying objects and not to touch drone debris, as this could contain "explosive elements".

In a statement on social media, the police said it had received several calls from residents of Chisinau and the surrounding area reporting the sound of explosions.

Moldovan President Maia Sandu criticised what she called "the boundless cynicism of Moscow's leaders" and vowed to continue supporting Kyiv.

European leaders should talk to Putin directly, Finnish president says

Finland's President Alexander Stubb urged European leaders to speak directly with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in an interview with the Financial Times on Tuesday.

Outsourcing talks with Russia to the US was not a responsible course of action, according to Stubb's comments to the business paper.

Stubb and Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store held a "frank and substantive" phone call in October with Putin about efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

Europe has been readying itself to take direct part in talks on ending Moscow's war after US envoys said last week that the Kremlin had agreed to let it join.

EU leaders last week agreed that France, along with Britain, Germany, Italy, Poland and the EU institutions should represent Europe.

Russian drone flew over Moldovan capital, president says

Moldovan President Maia Sandu said on Tuesday that a Russian drone flew over the capital Chisinau and pledged to press for further sanctions on Moscow.

"This evening several Russian drones violated our airspace, one of them over Chisinau, alarming residents," Sandu wrote on X.

"Russia's war threatens all of Europe. Moldova stands for peace. We'll keep pushing for sanctions on Moscow, standing with Ukraine and building our defence with partners.

© AP Photo

Top US official criticises Ukraine's 'deep strikes' against Russia, citing escalation risk

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia Tuesday, saying they "have not been effective in driving an end to the war" or in blunting Russia's advances.

"Such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate," Colby told a gathering of Ukraine's backers at NATO headquarters in Brussels, referring to a Russian e-commerce giant targeted by Kyiv.

French troops in Ukraine a 'direct participation' in conflict, Russia says

Russia said Tuesday it was aware of French troops having been sent to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris.

"Not only French ones, we know this. We have conveyed our concern... this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war," Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told reporters.

His remarks come a day after a source told AFP and other media that French soldiers had been operating in Ukraine for several months to train Ukrainian personnel and help maintain equipment.

A source told AFP earlier the mission of a small contingent of French troops excludes any combat role.

French troops in Ukraine a 'direct participation' in conflit, Russia says

Russia said Tuesday it was aware of French troops having been sent to Ukraine, calling it "direct participation" in the war and saying a message had been issued to Paris.

"Not only French ones, we know this. We have conveyed our concern... this is no longer support for Ukraine, but direct participation in the war," Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov told reporters.

His remarks come a day after a source told AFP and other media that French soldiers had been operating in Ukraine for several months to train Ukrainian personnel and help maintain equipment.

A source told AFP earlier the mission of a small contingent of French troops excludes any combat role.

They spoke on condition of anonymity after Radio France Internationale (RFI) first revealed the presence of French troops in the war-torn country earlier Monday.

France rejects 'absurd' Russian claim French troops participating in Ukraine war

France on Tuesday rejected as "absurd" a claim by the Russian foreign minister that a contingent of French troops deployed in Ukraine were directly involved in fighting against Moscow.

There is a "very limited" deployment of French troops in Ukraine for training and equipment maintenance, deputy defence minister Alice Rufo told parliament. But "there is the absence of any intention to fight, contrary to what the Russian foreign minister (Sergei Lavrov) said this morning, which is absurd."

Ukraine offers humanitarian mission for 10 settlements, Zelensky says

Ukraine has offered to carry out a humanitarian mission similar to the one in Russia-occupied Oleshky for 10 settlements in the southern Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

"Our team will discuss this with the American mediators," he said on X.

Defence minister: Ukraine's military hit 14 Russian ballistic missile launchers in recent weeks

Ukraine, Russia hit key bridges ahead of Putin-Xi-Trump summit

Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

Finland's president says clear timeline, agenda important for Russia-Ukraine negotiations

Finland's President Alexander Stubb said on Tuesday it was important to get a clear timetable and agenda for the negotiations between Russia and Ukraine.

Russia will continue fuel imports, Kremlin says

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak has told a meeting of government representatives, oil producers and other officials to continue work to secure fuel imports, the Kremlin announced in a statement.

Russia, normally one of the world's largest fuel exporters, had to start importing gasoline and other oil products last summer following a spate of Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil refineries.

Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles

Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.

Estonia to send 70 locomotives to Ukraine

Estonia is planning to send more than 70 locomotives to Ukraine to help maintain its railway network amid intensifying Russian attacks, Kyiv Independent reported, citing Estonia’s Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna.

The first deliveries could arrive before the end of this year, he said.

Ukraine says it has hit Salavat oil refinery in Russia's Bashkortostan

Ukraine's military said on Tuesday it had struck the Salavat oil refinery and petrochemical complex in Russia's Bashkortostan region.

In a post on Telegram, the General Staff said the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat plant was hit overnight, about 1,500 km (930 miles) from the Ukrainian border and that explosions were heard and a fire broke out at the site.

"Salavat is no ordinary plant. It is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical complexes, capable of processing about 10 million tonnes of oil a year," it said.

Hungary-Ukraine Railway traffic suspended after Russian drone attack

Hungary is suspending railway traffic to and from Ukraine on Tuesday and Wednesday after a Russian drone attack in western Ukraine, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar wrote in a Facebook post on Tuesday.

Magyar said the decision was made after a Russian drone struck a location 300 meters from the railway station in the town of Mukachevo.

Crimea Bridge closed to road traffic after strikes cause partial collapse: Ukrainian military

The Ukrainian military has said that the Crimea Bridge is closed to road traffic after drone and missile strikes caused a road section of the bridge to collapse, falling into the water below.

Strikes also damaged a railway arch it added.

"For the occupiers, this is more than a symbolic blow. The bridge was the main artery carrying fuel, ammunition, equipment and personnel to the peninsula and on into southern Ukraine... The occupiers are left with fewer and fewer land routes to Crimea," it added.

- Ukraine for the second day in a row hit a symbolic bridge that links the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia, a Moscow-installed official said Tuesday.

- Russian President Vladimir Putin could meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-Un if he also attends this week's APEC summit in China, Interfax news agency quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying on Monday.

- Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky says intelligence shows that Russia is planning new strikes on Ukrainian targets Monday evening, overnight and Tuesday, according to a report by Reuters.

(FRANCE 24 with AP, AFP and Reuters)
articles.title: Путин прибыл в Китай в преддверии трехстороннего саммита Трампа-Си
articles.text: Президент России Владимир Путин в среду прибыл в Китай, где, как ожидается, встретится со своими американскими и китайскими коллегами Дональдом Трампом и Си Цзиньпином в кулуарах саммита АТЭС, сообщают российские государственные СМИ. Российское государственное информационное агентство ТАСС сообщило, что самолет Путина приземлился в международном аэропорту Баоань в Шэньчжэне. Путин примет участие в саммите на этой неделе. Следите за нашим блогом для последних событий.

articles.originalTitle: Africa: Trading in yuan
articles.originalText: The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.
articles.originalFullText:
The dollar has long ruled Africa's financial landscape. But as more countries turn to China's yuan, the balance of economic power could be shifting.

SACHA PFEIFFER, HOST:

President Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China next week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic summit. The meeting is likely to be overshadowed by allegations that the head of U.S. chipmaker Nvidia, Jensen Huang, had an affair with a Chinese spy. The U.S. and China are in the midst of an AI race, and the two countries are also competing on many other fronts, including in mineral-rich Africa, as Kate Bartlett reports from Johannesburg.

KATE BARTLETT, BYLINE: In Africa, the greenback has long been king.

(SOUNDBITE OF BELL RINGING)

UNIDENTIFIED CROWD: Woohoo.

(CHEERING)

BARTLETT: Zimbabwe's Victoria Falls Stock Exchange trades exclusively in U.S. dollars, and most everyday transactions on the street are also in dollars, a legacy of the hyperinflation that devastated the country's own currency two decades ago.

(SOUNDBITE OF STREET AMBIANCE)

BARTLETT: Directly across the border in Zambia, it's long been a similar situation, but this is changing, as this recent Zambian government advert points out.

(SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING)

UNIDENTIFIED COMMENTATOR: Zambia has officially become the first African nation to accept China's yuans, also known as RMB, for the payment of mine taxes and royalties.

BARTLETT: And it's not only Zambia that's conducting business in RMB. China is, by far, Africa's biggest trading partner, and now more and more African countries are turning to the Chinese yuan for trade and to pay their debt. According to Cobus van Staden, a China expert at the South Africa (ph) Institute of International Affairs in Johannesburg, the trend reflects China's growing influence across the continent.

COBUS VAN STADEN: The interesting thing is going to be whether this starts to chip away at dollar dominance in certain specific commodity fields, whether increasingly, we're going to be looking at lithium or copper or cobalt and see those fields becoming more and more de-dollarized over time. We'll have to see.

BARTLETT: These are some of the critical minerals the U.S. and China are competing for on the continent. Christian-Géraud Neema is an editor with the China-Global South Project, an Africa-based think tank which tracks Beijing's influence across the continent. He points out several African countries, like Kenya, have already restructured their debt to China and are now paying it in yuan rather than dollars.

CHRISTIAN-GÉRAUD NEEMA: When you have China as your main trade partners, it really just makes sense for many African countries now to starting to trade with China in renminbi instead of trading with China in U.S. dollar.

BARTLETT: Paul Nantulya, of the Africa Center for Strategic Studies in Washington, points to another sign of the yuan's growing reach. More major African banks are now offering direct yuan payments and currency conversion, like South Africa's Standard Bank.

PAUL NANTULYA: It is expanding. It is growing. I expect it to continue growing over the next five to 10 years.

BARTLETT: That's attractive to importers and exporters on the continent as it saves them double conversion costs. The Trump administration's shifting tariff policies have only strengthened the case for African businesses to diversify away from the dollar. Still, Nantulya is circumspect.

NANTULYA: I don't think you're going to see a rapid departure from the use of the U.S. dollar, however. What I think you're going to see instead, and what you're already seeing right now, is diversification.

BARTLETT: In other words, the dollar isn't about to be displaced, but across Africa, the alternatives are rapidly gaining ground.

Kate Bartlett, NPR News, Johannesburg.

(SOUNDBITE OF RONNIE FOSTER'S "MYSTIC BREW")

Доллар долгое время управлял финансовым ландшафтом Африки. Но по мере того, как все больше стран обращаются к юаню Китая, баланс экономической мощи может измениться.

Саша Файффер, ведущий:

Президент Трамп встретится с президентом Китая Си Цзиньпином в Китае на следующей неделе в кулуарах Азиатско-Тихоокеанского экономического саммита. Встреча, вероятно, будет омрачена утверждениями о том, что глава американского производителя чипов Nvidia Дженсен Хуанг имел роман с китайским шпионом. США и Китай находятся в разгаре гонки ИИ, и обе страны также конкурируют на многих других фронтах, в том числе в богатой полезными ископаемыми Африке.

Кейт Бартлетт: В Африке гринбек давно стал королем.

(Звук колокола звонит)

Неизвестный преступник: Вуху.

(Смеется)

Биржа Виктория-Фолс в Зимбабве торгуется исключительно в долларах США, и большинство ежедневных транзакций на улице также осуществляются в долларах, наследие гиперинфляции, которая опустошила собственную валюту страны два десятилетия назад.

(Саундбайт Уличного Дружбы)

БАРТЛЕТТ: Прямо через границу в Замбии уже давно сложилась аналогичная ситуация, но она меняется, как указывается в недавней рекламе правительства Замбии.

(СУНДБИТ АРХИВИДНОЙ РЕКОРДИИ)

Замбия официально стала первой африканской страной, принявшей китайские юани, также известные как юань, для уплаты налогов и роялти.

И не только Замбия ведет бизнес в юанях. Китай, безусловно, является крупнейшим торговым партнером Африки, и теперь все больше и больше африканских стран обращаются к китайскому юаню за торговлей и погашают свой долг. По словам Кобуса ван Стадена, эксперта по Китаю из Южно-Африканского института международных отношений в Йоханнесбурге, эта тенденция отражает растущее влияние Китая на континенте.

Интересно, начнет ли это ослаблять доминирование доллара в определенных конкретных товарных полях, все чаще мы будем смотреть на литий, медь или кобальт и увидим, что эти поля со временем становятся все более и более дедолларизированными. Мы должны увидеть.

Вот некоторые из важнейших полезных ископаемых, за которые США и Китай конкурируют на континенте. Кристиан-Жоро Неема является редактором Китайско-глобального южного проекта, африканского аналитического центра, который отслеживает влияние Пекина на континенте. Он указывает, что несколько африканских стран, таких как Кения, уже реструктурировали свой долг перед Китаем и теперь платят его в юанях, а не в долларах.

ХРИСТИАН-ГЕРАУД НЕЕМА: Когда у вас есть Китай в качестве основных торговых партнеров, для многих африканских стран сейчас имеет смысл начать торговать с Китаем в юанях, а не торговать с Китаем в долларах США.

Пол Нантулия из Африканского центра стратегических исследований в Вашингтоне указывает на еще один признак растущего охвата юаня. Более крупные африканские банки в настоящее время предлагают прямые платежи в юанях и конвертацию валюты, такие как южноафриканский Standard Bank.

Пол Нантулия: Она расширяется. Она растет. Я ожидаю, что он продолжит расти в течение следующих пяти-10 лет.

Это привлекательно для импортеров и экспортеров на континенте, поскольку это экономит им двойные затраты на конверсию. Смена тарифной политики администрации Трампа только укрепила позиции африканских компаний по диверсификации от доллара. Тем не менее, Нантулия осмотрительна.

Я не думаю, что вы увидите быстрый отход от использования доллара США. Я думаю, что вместо этого вы увидите, и то, что вы уже видите сейчас, это диверсификация.

Другими словами, доллар не собирается вытесняться, но по всей Африке альтернативы быстро набирают силу.

Кейт Бартлетт, NPR News, Йоханнесбург.

articles.originalTitle: California sues OpenAI over hacking risks
articles.originalText: The state's attorney general started investigating OpenAI after the Hugging Face attack and now says this attack was "entirely foreseeable" due to OpenAI's poor security practices.
articles.originalFullText:
California sued OpenAI Monday, alleging that the frontier AI company failed to protect the public from its systems' advanced cyber capabilities. The lawsuit stems from OpenAI's agents' attack on open-source software platform Hugging Face over the summer but also touches on a wide range of other related incidents tied to the company's agents acting without authorization.

"Just because the technology is new or rapidly evolving doesn't mean the people behind it are above the law," said California Attorney General Rob Bonta during a press conference. "Whether it's a car or a toy, the law is simple: don't build or test things that can hurt people without proper safeguards." The lawsuit cited potential concerns about cyberattacks "on power grids, emergency infrastructure, hospital systems, and financial institutions."

In the complaint, California alleged that OpenAI misled the public about how unsafe its products are. The state said the company admitted to the attorney general's office that "it lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing."

That number is higher than what OpenAI has so far disclosed publicly and more than what outside researchers have independently discovered, but OpenAI has otherwise provided little information, California said. The state also accused OpenAI of poor security practices, stonewalling the state's investigation into the company and discouraging employees from speaking up about safety.

In a statement to NPR, OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri said the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab" and that the company has "engaged—and will continue to engage—constructively with the Attorney General's office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry."

After the most notorious of cyber incidents involving OpenAI's agents – the attack on Hugging Face over the summer – the company admitted that it did not monitor its agents in ways its own researchers deemed important. Since then, outside researchers as well as OpenAI itself have found more incidents in which AI agents have interacted with websites and communicated with each other on the internet in ways that OpenAI did not intend. The lawsuit mentions these events as well as other incidents that OpenAI started disclosing voluntarily to the public.

Other AI companies have also had to wrestle with their systems behaving in unexpected and undesirable ways. Anthropic and Meta have both said they found that their AI systems have hacked into places they shouldn't have. Major AI companies have since signed onto an agreement organized by the White House to develop AI responsibly, but the agreement is nonbinding.

Drawing from reports including from OpenAI's own disclosures, California alleges that the top AI company has engaged in unfair competition and created a public nuisance. It asked the court to stop the company from further engaging in such activities and order it to pay monetary damages.
articles.fullText:
Калифорния подала в суд на OpenAI в понедельник, утверждая, что пограничная компания ИИ не смогла защитить общественность от передовых кибер-возможностей своих систем. Иск связан с атакой агентов OpenAI на программную платформу с открытым исходным кодом Hugging Face в течение лета, но также затрагивает широкий спектр других связанных инцидентов, связанных с агентами компании, действующими без разрешения.

«То, что технология является новой или быстро развивается, не означает, что люди, стоящие за ней, выше закона», — сказал генеральный прокурор Калифорнии Роб Бонта. Будь то автомобиль или игрушка, закон прост: не стройте и не тестируйте вещи, которые могут навредить людям без надлежащих гарантий. В иске упоминались потенциальные опасения по поводу кибератак «на электросети, аварийную инфраструктуру, системы больниц и финансовые учреждения».

В жалобе Калифорния утверждала, что OpenAI ввела общественность в заблуждение о том, насколько небезопасны ее продукты. В заявлении говорится, что компания призналась генеральному прокурору, что «в ходе тестирования она более 80 раз теряла контроль над своими автономными агентами ИИ».

Это число выше, чем то, что OpenAI до сих пор публично раскрывал, и больше, чем то, что независимые исследователи обнаружили, но OpenAI в противном случае предоставил мало информации. Государство также обвинило OpenAI в плохой практике обеспечения безопасности, блокируя расследование штата в отношении компании и не позволяя сотрудникам говорить о безопасности.

В заявлении для NPR представитель OpenAI Дрю Пусатери сказал, что иск «похоже, выделяет OpenAI по проблеме, которая была идентифицирована каждой крупной лабораторией ИИ», и что компания «взаимодействовала и будет продолжать конструктивно взаимодействовать с Генеральной прокуратурой, чтобы делиться информацией и продвигать сильные, практические стандарты безопасности для всей отрасли».

После самого печально известного из кибер-инцидентов с участием агентов OpenAI - атаки на Hugging Face в течение лета - компания признала, что не следила за своими агентами способами, которые ее собственные исследователи считали важными. С тех пор внешние исследователи, а также сам OpenAI обнаружили больше инцидентов, в которых агенты ИИ взаимодействовали с веб-сайтами и общались друг с другом в Интернете способами, которые OpenAI не намеревался. В иске упоминаются эти события, а также другие инциденты, которые OpenAI начал добровольно раскрывать общественности.

Другие компании, занимающиеся ИИ, также вынуждены бороться с тем, что их системы ведут себя неожиданным и нежелательным образом. Антропик и Мета заявили, что их системы ИИ взломали места, которые они не должны были иметь. С тех пор крупные компании, занимающиеся ИИ, подписали соглашение, организованное Белым домом для ответственного развития ИИ, но соглашение не имеет обязательной силы.

Основываясь на отчетах, в том числе на собственных раскрытиях OpenAI, Калифорния утверждает, что топ-компания AI занималась недобросовестной конкуренцией и создавала общественные неприятности. Он попросил суд остановить компанию от дальнейшего участия в такой деятельности и обязать ее выплатить денежный ущерб.

articles.originalTitle: Hard bargain: Should Ukraine trade Donbas for NATO membership?
articles.originalText: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap: Russia gets the Donbas and the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership – a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer is real, serious or either side would accept it is another matter. We ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's at a brutal stalemate.
articles.originalFullText:
President Volodymyr Zelensky asserting that the United States has asked him about a straight-up swap Russia gets the Donbas, the rest of Ukraine gets NATO membership, a guarantee against Moscow later having a second go and annexing the entire country. Whether or not the offer’s real, serious or that either side would accept it. We’ll ask if the talk of partition signals some kind of turning point in a nearly five-year war that's also a brutal stalemate.

The remarks came just days ahead of a three-way summit in Shenzhen, China that some have likened to Yalta, the 1945 carving up of Europe between the Soviets and Anglo-Americans. A fair comparison? From weekend border tensions between Russia and Estonia to EU leaders’ inability to agree on a single name to represent the bloc in Ukraine war talks, we’ll ask what this crucial week means for the future of the continent, where some of Ukraine's strongest backers may be on borrowed time. Enter French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen, the far-right leader whose 2017 campaign was financed by a Russian bank. She knows a majority of her compatriots support Ukraine, hence a courtesy call this Monday to its ambassador in Paris. But after she repeated that if elected, she'll pull the plug on financing for Kyiv.

Produced by Rebecca Gnignati, Elisa Amiri, Ilayda Habip.

Президент Владимир Зеленский утверждает, что Соединенные Штаты спросили его о прямом обмене Россией Донбасса, остальная часть Украины получает членство в НАТО, гарантию против того, чтобы Москва позже получила второй шанс и аннексировала всю страну. Будет ли предложение реальным, серьезным или любая из сторон примет его. Мы спросим, сигнализирует ли разговор о разделе о каком-то поворотном моменте в почти пятилетней войне, которая также является жестоким тупиком.

Замечания прозвучали всего за несколько дней до трехстороннего саммита в Шэньчжэне, Китай, который некоторые сравнивают с Ялтой, разделившей Европу в 1945 году между Советами и англо-американцами. Справедливое сравнение? От напряженности на границе между Россией и Эстонией до неспособности лидеров ЕС договориться о едином названии, чтобы представлять блок на переговорах по войне в Украине, мы спросим, что эта важная неделя означает для будущего континента, где некоторые из самых сильных сторонников Украины могут быть в заемное время. Войдите во французский президентский лидер Марин Ле Пен, крайне правый лидер, чья кампания 2017 года финансировалась российским банком. Она знает, что большинство ее соотечественников поддерживают Украину, поэтому в понедельник вежливо позвонит ее послу в Париже. Но после того, как она повторит, что в случае избрания, она отключит финансирование для Киева.

articles.originalTitle: U.S. tightens controls on remote access to AI technology amid Nvidia fallout
articles.originalText: The new rule closes a loophole that existed that allowed Chinese companies to still access advanced AI chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.
articles.originalFullText:
The U.S. government has announced a rule to prevent remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and servers, closing a loophole that could let adversarial governments access American AI technology through overseas data centers.

The move comes amid the fallout at Nvidia, the world's dominant producer of AI chips, following revelations that CEO Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with a woman who U.S. intelligence officials suspected of being a Chinese intelligence operative. NPR has not independently verified the claims. Huang stepped down as CEO last week.

Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, is a former executive at Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based data center company. Jensen Huang has personally lobbied President Trump to loosen restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China. It is not known if Alice Huang influenced this activity.

The rapid advancement in cloud computing and AI infrastructure has made it possible to access advanced U.S. computing capabilities remotely, including through data centers located outside countries subject to U.S. export restrictions, the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) said in a statement on Monday.

The rule is designed to reinforce existing restrictions on access to sensitive American AI technology through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in other countries, which could threaten national security

However, a loophole existed where Chinese companies could still access those chips remotely, despite U.S. restrictions on their physical sale to China.

"The United States is the global leader in advanced computing and super intelligence technology and is committed to promoting the global adoption of American technology for legitimate commercial purposes while ensuring that sensitive technologies are not exploited in ways that threaten U.S. national security," the BIS statement said.

The government refers to artificial intelligence as "super intelligence" following an executive order signed by President Trump in September.

Since October 2022, U.S. companies have typically needed a BIS export license to sell advanced computing chips meeting specified technical thresholds to China, including Hong Kong and Macau. These restrictions covered advanced Nvidia chips, some high-performance semiconductor components, and certain AI computing systems.

Megaspeed is based in Singapore and operates facilities in Malaysia.

"Megaspeed conducts legitimate and lawful business. The company has retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation," the company said in a statement emailed to NPR and other news organizations on Sunday.

Prior to the Nvidia scandal, the Trump administration had resisted imposing additional regulations to prevent foreign access to American AI technology.

The Biden administration had written a framework designed to control worldwide distribution of advanced AI chips on January 15, 2025 – five days before Trump's inauguration. In May 2025, Trump's Commerce Department announced it would not enforce the rule and intended to rescind it, calling it "ill-conceived and counterproductive."

Biden's framework would have also limited access to AI chips by countries considered security risks, required licenses for certain chip exports, and created restrictions on the power of advanced models and computing infrastructure.

The New York Times reported that Trump was first briefed by intelligence officials about Jensen Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy in October 2025. Both Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are expected to testify before Congress this month and next month and there will likely be further investigations into what Trump knew about the affair when the Democrats take control of Congress in January 2027, Rep. Yvette Clarke, D-NY, told NPR.

"We need to get the facts investigated, bring in individuals to give us as much information as possible under oath, so that we can get to the bottom of why this happened, how it occurred, and how we could prevent this type of compromise from happening again," said Clarke.

Правительство США объявило о правиле предотвращения удаленного доступа к передовым чипам и серверам искусственного интеллекта, закрыв лазейку, которая может позволить правительствам-противникам получить доступ к американской технологии ИИ через зарубежные центры обработки данных.

Этот шаг происходит на фоне последствий в Nvidia, доминирующем в мире производителе чипов ИИ, после откровений о том, что генеральный директор Дженсен Хуанг имел романтические отношения с женщиной, которую сотрудники разведки США подозревали в том, что она является агентом китайской разведки. NPR не проверяла эти утверждения независимо. Хуан ушел с поста генерального директора на прошлой неделе.

Элис Хуан, которая не имеет отношения к Дженсену Хуангу, является бывшим руководителем компании Megaspeed International, расположенной в Сингапуре. Дженсен Хуан лично лоббировал президента Трампа, чтобы ослабить ограничения на продажи чипов Nvidia в Китай. Неизвестно, повлияла ли на эту деятельность Алиса Хуан.

Быстрое развитие облачных вычислений и инфраструктуры ИИ позволило получить удаленный доступ к передовым вычислительным возможностям США, в том числе через центры обработки данных, расположенные за пределами стран, на которые распространяются экспортные ограничения США, говорится в заявлении Бюро промышленности и безопасности Министерства торговли США (BIS).

Данное правило призвано усилить существующие ограничения на доступ к чувствительным американским технологиям искусственного интеллекта посредством удаленных вычислений с участием центров обработки данных в других странах, которые могут угрожать национальной безопасности.

Тем не менее, существует лазейка, в которой китайские компании все еще могут получить доступ к этим чипам удаленно, несмотря на ограничения США на их физическую продажу в Китай.

«Соединенные Штаты являются мировым лидером в области передовых вычислительных и сверхразведывательных технологий и привержены продвижению глобального внедрения американских технологий в законных коммерческих целях, обеспечивая при этом, чтобы чувствительные технологии не использовались таким образом, который угрожает национальной безопасности США», — говорится в заявлении BIS.

Правительство называет искусственный интеллект «супер-интеллектом» в соответствии с распоряжением, подписанным президентом Трампом в сентябре.

С октября 2022 года американским компаниям, как правило, нужна экспортная лицензия BIS для продажи передовых вычислительных чипов, отвечающих определенным техническим порогам, в Китай, включая Гонконг и Макао. Эти ограничения касались передовых чипов Nvidia, некоторых высокопроизводительных полупроводниковых компонентов и некоторых вычислительных систем ИИ.

Megaspeed базируется в Сингапуре и управляет объектами в Малайзии.

"Мегаспид ведет законные и законные дела. Компания сохранила внешнего адвоката для проведения тщательного внутреннего расследования, - говорится в заявлении компании, направленном в воскресенье в NPR и другие новостные организации.

До скандала с Nvidia администрация Трампа сопротивлялась введению дополнительных правил для предотвращения иностранного доступа к американским технологиям искусственного интеллекта.

Администрация Байдена написала структуру, предназначенную для контроля за распространением передовых чипов искусственного интеллекта во всем мире 15 января 2025 года, за пять дней до инаугурации Трампа. В мае 2025 года министерство торговли Трампа объявило, что не будет применять правило и намерено отменить его, назвав его «непродуманным и контрпродуктивным».

Структура Байдена также ограничила бы доступ к чипам искусственного интеллекта странами, которые считают риски для безопасности, потребовала бы лицензий на определенный экспорт чипов и создала бы ограничения на мощность передовых моделей и вычислительной инфраструктуры.

The New York Times сообщила, что Трамп был впервые проинформирован сотрудниками разведки о романе Дженсена Хуанга с подозреваемым китайским шпионом в октябре 2025 года. Ожидается, что и Дженсен Хуанг, и министр торговли Говард Лютник дадут показания перед Конгрессом в этом месяце и в следующем месяце, и, вероятно, будут проведены дальнейшие расследования того, что Трамп знал о романе, когда демократы возьмут под контроль Конгресс в январе 2027 года, сказала представитель Иветт Кларк, D-NY.

«Нам нужно расследовать факты, привлекать людей, чтобы дать нам как можно больше информации под присягой, чтобы мы могли понять, почему это произошло, как это произошло и как мы могли бы предотвратить повторение такого рода компромисса», — сказал Кларк.

Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said.

As hundreds of thousands of people gather in Prague to protest the Czech government's proposal to replace public broadcasting licence fees with direct state funding, Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Bára Stárek, Executive Director of Díky, že můžem. Stárek warns that the proposed changes offer "no real safeguards" against political influence, pointing to developments in Slovakia and Hungary. She also drew a parallel with the Velvet Revolution of 1989, recalling that "we didn't have a free media and we only had a state media" under communist rule. "Media is the first (line of) attack when you want to attack democracy," she said. With the legislation expected to reach Parliament in January, Stárek believes the demonstrations will continue if the government refuses to engage in any discussions.

articles.originalTitle: U.N. talks seek to rein in 'killer robots' as fears over AI weapons grow
articles.originalText: Countries are meeting in Geneva to negotiate rules on weapons that can select and kill targets without human intervention. But with the U.S., Russia and Israel resisting legally binding controls, campaigners fear the window to act is closing.
articles.originalFullText:
GENEVA — Negotiations on possible rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, also known as 'killer robots' are underway at the United Nations in Geneva.

Supporters of controls on autonomous weapons say this week's U.N. conference on Certain Conventional Weapons (or CCW), which meets just once every five years, is the last best chance to agree rules before it is too late.

Warfare technology has advanced rapidly in the last few years, with some experts warning that the world is just months away from having weapons that can choose targets and make the decision to kill autonomously.

In Ukraine and Gaza, AI-assisted weapons have already been used to take out targets, with Ukrainian civilians reporting being 'hunted' by drones as they shop or go to school. But these are still controlled remotely by humans.

Humanitarian organizations say the decision to kill – and responsibility for that choice – must stay in human hands. Ahead of this week's meeting, the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Pope have all called for legally binding rules. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that allowing fully autonomous weapons to kill would be 'crossing a moral red line'.

What are the risks?

The Red Cross is especially worried that existing rules of war – the Geneva Conventions – cannot be fully respected by autonomous weapons. War is often chaotic and confusing, and the situation can change rapidly. Under the Conventions, soldiers who are wounded or in the process of surrendering can no longer be targeted.

Georgia Haines, a legal adviser with the Red Cross, worries that autonomous weapons will not be able to distinguish between a soldier who is still fighting, one who is wounded and one who wants to surrender.

'The risk is that, based on the technology we are seeing, they are not able to understand in the same way that a human is the contextual signals. And so the risks are incredibly high that there will be a misidentification of a target.'

Meanwhile, human rights groups warn that the technology behind AI-assisted weapons is becoming increasingly cheap and easy to use. The more it is adopted by the military, the greater the danger of proliferation and its use by terrorist groups or law enforcement agencies in repressive regimes. In theory, a swarm of autonomous drones could be programmed to kill everyone wearing a red sweater, everyone carrying a poster or even everyone speaking a certain language.

Many of the countries now meeting in Geneva take such concerns very seriously. At least 50, including Ireland, Italy, Brazil, Mexico, France and Germany, are calling for a strict timetable to agree on binding rules governing autonomous weapons.

But among states that are already developing and using semi-autonomous weapons, there is pushback. The United States, Russia and Israel have indicated they are set to oppose legally binding rules, with Washington proposing a five-year timetable to draft non-binding guidelines instead.

The U.S. is traditionally a late adopter of international treaties. It did not ratify the Ottawa Convention on landmines, for example, although it did, over time, stop deploying them and reduce its stockpiles.

Under President Trump, doubts about international law have grown. Washington has imposed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court, and just this weekend, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in a keynote speech to the Federalist Society, warned against "quoting laws to men with swords."

The problem for states meeting in Geneva is that U.N. negotiations on limiting specific weapons are supposed to be conducted by consensus. This was achieved in 1995, when countries agreed to a ban on blinding lasers, but other agreements have proved elusive. With landmines, countries frustrated by the delay finally took negotiations outside the U.N. process to create the Ottawa Convention.

This week, there may be a compromise: a longer or even open-ended negotiating period to come up with rules that individual states can adopt as binding or non-binding. For diplomats supporting such a solution, it is a way to ensure at least some progress. For campaigners, it is less than ideal, with one likening it to kicking a very dangerous can down the road.

Переговоры о возможных правилах использования летального автономного оружия, также известного как «роботы-убийцы», ведутся в Организации Объединенных Наций в Женеве.

Сторонники контроля над автономным оружием говорят, что конференция ООН по некоторым видам обычного оружия, которая проходит раз в пять лет, является последним шансом договориться о правилах, пока не стало слишком поздно.

В последние несколько лет технологии ведения войны быстро развивались, и некоторые эксперты предупреждают, что мир находится всего в нескольких месяцах от наличия оружия, которое может выбирать цели и принимать решение убивать автономно.

В Украине и Газе оружие с помощью искусственного интеллекта уже используется для уничтожения целей, а украинские гражданские лица сообщают, что их «охотят» беспилотники, когда они совершают покупки или ходят в школу. Но они все еще контролируются дистанционно людьми.

Гуманитарные организации говорят, что решение убивать и ответственность за этот выбор должны оставаться в человеческих руках. В преддверии встречи на этой неделе ООН, Международный комитет Красного Креста и Папа Римский призвали к юридически обязательным правилам. Генеральный секретарь ООН Антониу Гутерриш предупредил, что разрешение полностью автономного оружия на убийство будет «пересекать моральную красную линию».

Каковы риски?

Красный Крест особенно обеспокоен тем, что существующие правила войны - Женевские конвенции - не могут быть полностью соблюдены автономным оружием. Война часто хаотична и запутанна, и ситуация может быстро измениться. Согласно Конвенции, солдаты, которые получили ранения или находятся в процессе капитуляции, больше не могут быть мишенью.

Джорджия Хейнс, юрисконсульт Красного Креста, опасается, что автономное оружие не сможет отличить солдата, который все еще воюет, того, кто ранен, от того, кто хочет сдаться.

Риск заключается в том, что, основываясь на технологии, которую мы видим, они не могут понять так же, как человек является контекстуальным сигналом. И поэтому риски невероятно высоки, что будет неправильное определение цели.

Между тем, правозащитные организации предупреждают, что технология, лежащая в основе оружия с искусственным интеллектом, становится все более дешевой и простой в использовании. Чем больше она принимается военными, тем больше опасность распространения и ее использования террористическими группами или правоохранительными органами в репрессивных режимах. Теоретически, рой автономных дронов может быть запрограммирован на то, чтобы убить всех, кто носит красный свитер, всех, кто носит плакат или даже всех, кто говорит на определенном языке.

Многие из стран, которые сейчас встречаются в Женеве, относятся к этим проблемам очень серьезно. По меньшей мере 50 стран, включая Ирландию, Италию, Бразилию, Мексику, Францию и Германию, призывают к строгому графику согласования обязательных правил, регулирующих автономное оружие.

Но среди государств, которые уже разрабатывают и используют полуавтономное оружие, есть отпор. Соединенные Штаты, Россия и Израиль заявили, что они намерены выступить против юридически обязательных правил, а Вашингтон предлагает вместо этого пятилетний график разработки необязательных руководящих принципов.

Соединенные Штаты традиционно являются поздним сторонником международных договоров. Например, она не ратифицировала Оттавскую конвенцию о наземных минах, хотя со временем прекратила их развертывание и сократила свои запасы.

При президенте Трампе усилились сомнения в международном праве. Вашингтон ввел широкие санкции в отношении Международного уголовного суда, и только в эти выходные государственный секретарь Марко Рубио в своей программной речи перед федералистским обществом предостерег от «цитирования законов людям с мечами».

Проблема для государств, собравшихся в Женеве, заключается в том, что переговоры ООН по ограничению конкретных вооружений должны вестись консенсусом. Это было достигнуто в 1995 году, когда страны договорились о запрете ослепляющих лазеров, но другие соглашения оказались неуловимыми. С наземными минами страны, разочарованные задержкой, наконец, вышли на переговоры за пределы процесса ООН по созданию Оттавской конвенции.

На этой неделе может быть компромисс: более длительный или даже открытый период переговоров, чтобы придумать правила, которые отдельные государства могут принять в качестве обязательных или необязательных. Для дипломатов, поддерживающих такое решение, это способ обеспечить хоть какой-то прогресс. Для участников кампании это менее чем идеально, с одним уподоблением его удару очень опасной банки по дороге.
articles.title: Переговоры ООН стремятся обуздать «роботов-убийц», поскольку растут опасения по поводу оружия ИИ
articles.text: Страны встречаются в Женеве, чтобы обсудить правила по оружию, которое может выбирать и убивать цели без вмешательства человека. Но поскольку США, Россия и Израиль сопротивляются юридически обязывающему контролю, активисты опасаются, что окно для действий закрывается.

articles.originalTitle: Nearly two million people are behind bars in the US. How did we get here?
articles.originalText: Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America, goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how our approach to criminals has changed over time.
articles.originalFullText:
Lynn Novick's new, four-part PBS documentary series, Crime and Punishment in America, goes inside the U.S. prison system and explores how

our approach to criminals has changed over time.

DAVE DAVIES, HOST:

This is FRESH AIR. I'm Dave Davies. You might remember the controversy surrounding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's plan to livestream the execution of the man convicted of a mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas. The livestreaming plan was called off, but in colonial times, executions of criminals were among the largest public gatherings. Eight thousand people converged on Boston in 1773 to witness the hanging of Levi Ames, convicted of multiple acts of burglary. That story is among the revelations in a remarkable documentary series about crime and punishment in America coming to PBS this week, directed by our guest today, Lynn Novick.

The four-part series takes us from a day when prisons were largely unknown to the America of today, where nearly 2 million people are behind bars, a rate far higher than other industrialized countries. There are stories of criminal defendants, both innocent and guilty, as well as victims, police, prosecutors, judges and countless politicians who staked their fortunes on fighting crime. It raises critical questions and explores multiple points of view about how to answer them.

Lynn Novick is an award-winning documentary filmmaker who's collaborated with Ken Burns on many of his acclaimed series. Her most recent series, "College Behind Bars," was about men and women earning college degrees while incarcerated. Her series "Crime And Punishment In America" will air over four consecutive nights on PBS beginning tonight.

Lynn Novick, welcome back to FRESH AIR.

LYNN NOVICK: Thank you so much for having me, Dave. It's a pleasure to be here.

DAVIES: You know, you could do a long documentary series on crime in post-war America, or crime since the '90s, or crime in urban areas, or - I mean, in this case, you really take on a lot, going back to the beginning of the Republic. How did you come to decide to take on such a sprawling subject?

NOVICK: Yeah, it is a sprawling subject. For me, it felt like an opportunity to revisit the last 250 years of American history, which we have explored in other projects I've worked on with Ken Burns - history of jazz, history of baseball most notably - where we take a topic, an idea, and we look at all of American history through that lens. And it felt like no one had done this before, and the way that we address crime and the way that we punish and how we - why we have prisons and why we incarcerate at the rate that we do, all of these things didn't just come out of nowhere. And I wanted to understand how we got here, and the only way to do that was to kind of go back to the beginning and follow the breadcrumbs, so to speak, wherever they would lead.

DAVIES: You know, going back to colonial times, punishment for crimes was typically physical and quite public. How likely back then would an ordinary citizen be to witness an execution sometime in his or her life?

NOVICK: Yeah. I was stunned to learn from a number of our scholars and experts that executions were common in colonial America for a whole range of crimes. Not just what we would think of today of very serious, violent crimes - murder, rape, etc. - but you could be put to death for burglary, adultery, blasphemy, you know, robbery - just a wide range of crimes. And from what we understand, most people in colonial America would have seen an execution at some point in their lifetime. That is staggering to me.

DAVIES: Was - I mean, was this because they - it was believed that this would deter crime, or was there simply just such an interest in these public executions?

NOVICK: I think the answer is both, truly - that we've always been fascinated by those who transgress, who don't follow the rules and who get caught and have to pay the price. So that's - and that's not just Americans. Human beings are (ph) always been interested in, you know, who are the outlaws, the criminals, and, you know, why did they do the thing they did? And we want to see them punished.

And why punishment was administered publicly was, I believe, partly to deter - that was the idea - to shame, to just sort of send a message to everyone about the power of the state. So there's - it's serving a - to sort of knit together the social structure, you know, to build community, I suppose - that this is what we as a community do to those who, you know, disobey our rules. But as it turns out, it could have a sort of undermining effect of all those things as well. A huge crowd could gather at an execution and they might sort of start rabble-rousing, and you might even have a riot, and people might get hurt or robbed in the process of getting sort of excited about the execution. They might identify with the person who was being put to death and feel that it was unjust.

And so by the time of the revolution, some of our Founding Fathers who were really studying the enlightenment and thinking about what do citizens deserve in a republic and what kind of rights we should have began to put forth the idea that this public punishment and the sort of barbaric nature of it was actually bad for the society as a whole and that we should come up with a better way of doing this.

DAVIES: Right. Well, one alternative to physical punishment is confinement, and that leads us to prisons. What were early prisons like?

NOVICK: Yeah. Well, early prisons were - I think it was an experiment. We were trying out different ideas. And there were several different ways that the people who were investing in this idea of a structure - a penitentiary or a prison - where you would go for a period of time, where you would be expected to repent and to learn useful skills and to come back to society a better person - what we would now call rehabilitation. Some prisons were built on that idea. Some prisons, like the Eastern State Penitentiary in Philadelphia, which is one of the most monumental structures in Jacksonian America - it opened in 1829 - it was...

DAVIES: And is still there (laughter).

NOVICK: And is still there. And I certainly urge anyone who's in earshot of this to visit. It's an incredible place. It's a museum, and you can really understand palpably, physically, what this place was like. It was built to accomplish one goal, which was perfect isolation. You were in your cell 24 hours a day, seven days a week. There was a little yard. You had your own private outdoor space you can go into for one hour a day, but you weren't supposed to talk to anyone. The staff would come and check on you, but that was basically it. And it was such extreme isolation. As we can now understand today, pure solitary confinement was extremely deleterious to the people that were confined there, and eventually they did modify the system. But that was one model of incarceration.

And another model was sort of a modification of that, where people were put in isolation at night, but during the day they were put to work. And they were put to work for two reasons. One, to help pay for the cost of operating this sort of enormous institution, which is not cheap, and the second is to teach them, in theory, good habits. So rehabilitation as an idea was somehow merged with forced labor and isolation. And if we think about those three things going together, I would say they really don't. And so we've always had kind of a conflict about what are we actually trying to accomplish with prisons and penitentiaries.

DAVIES: Well, among the earlier prisons, they discovered that they could fund the prison by having private employers use the inmates for work. I mean, factories, you know, ironing clothes, whatever. And they got to be large, right? There was a guy named Elam Lynds - am I saying that correctly?

NOVICK: Yes, that's correct. Yeah.

DAVIES: Who designed a prison in Auburn. And then there was the one that came to be known as Sing Sing - I guess that's from Ossining, New York, right?

NOVICK: Yeah.

DAVIES: Where a lot of prisoners were managed by relatively few guards. And you're right, or it appears in the documentary that this drew visits from Europe. A couple of French aristocrats wanted to see how this worked. What did they discover? How did they react?

NOVICK: Yeah, it was hard for me to imagine a world where there hadn't been prisons before. And so when America created this penitentiary system and people started hearing about it, they wanted to come here and see, oh, wow, maybe we should bring this back to France or England or Germany or, you know, another country.

And in the 1830s, two young French aristocrats, Alexis de Tocqueville and Gustave de Beaumont, came to America. They were charged by the French government to study our system and write a report to see if, you know, France should do the same thing. And what they discovered was a paradox, in a way, that the prison that they visited, Sing Sing and Eastern State and a few other prisons, were run with such extraordinary discipline that you didn't need that many guards or officers or, as they were called then, keepers to maintain control because anyone who broke the rules was punished brutally. So we - they interviewed Elam Lynds, who was the head keeper at Sing Sing, and he said, I don't think it's possible to govern a prison without a whip. And anyone who says otherwise doesn't understand human nature. And a whip isn't that bad. It doesn't hurt people that much, but, you know, the fear of being whipped is the only way that you can maintain control.

And so what we see right there - the penitentiary system is pretty new at that point - is that we had tried to create a system where we wouldn't brutalize people and that we wouldn't torture them. And instead, we would put them in a place where they could reform. But once they're in that place behind the walls, now we're torturing them again.

DAVIES: Right, right. And I believe some of these foreign visitors were kind of appalled with - by what they saw but saw that it was effective, and it did kind of spread, right?

NOVICK: Yes, exactly. They were appalled and impressed, if that's possible. Sort of appalled at what it took but also thinking, maybe this is worth trying, which - I find that's a paradox that's hard to square with the notion of democracy and, you know, people having rights. But I think one thing we have seen is that once people get found guilty of a crime and sent to prison, they are stripped of their rights and not treated the way they would be treated if they were, you know, in the free world and not confined.

DAVIES: You know, I was going to play a clip here that had to do with the kind of punishment that was in store for inmates who got out of line. There's a story of a career criminal who wrote a memoir, George Appo, quite a character, began as a kid, you know, kid of the streets. It's a fascinating story. He was sent as a teenager. He was arrested, and I think he didn't want to go to the juvenile place, which he thought was torturous. So he pretended to be older, and he got sent to Sing Sing. On his third day, when he was ironing a shirt, he burned it and was given the paddle. This was the punishment. And here's a clip from the documentary about that particular punishment. We're going to hear, first, a narrator describing what the paddle is and then historian Timothy Gilfoyle talking about it. Let's listen.

(SOUNDBITE OF DOCUMENTARY, "CRIME AND PUNISHMENT IN AMERICA")

(SOUNDBITE OF PADDLE STRIKING)

TIMOTHY GILFOYLE: The paddle. It would create a sense of terror, actually, on the part of people incarcerated in Sing Sing. One prison guard actually quit because when he would enter the cafeteria at night, he remembered seeing men that had been paddled literally crying at their tables, praying to the Virgin Mary because they were in such pain. Some men tried to commit suicide upon learning they were about to be paddled, jumping off from the third or fourth tiers of their cells.

DAVIES: And that's from the documentary directed by our guest Lynn Novick. So it was pretty brutal.

NOVICK: And, you know, I think it was brutal and it wasn't seen by the outside world. So we went from having punishment - brutal punishment administered in the town square to being administered behind the walls of a prison where people couldn't go who weren't, you know, in custody there. And one of the reasons why you would be punished is if you didn't do your work job well or you refused to work, or, you know, you didn't comply with a very strict regimen, the rules that were there, a lot of which had to do with you know, production for these outside employers, like you mentioned.

And so you bring a factory in - you build a factory inside the prison. People are supposed to work there eight to 10 hours a day, six days a week for no money. And if they refuse to work, the officers, the keepers, are doing the enforcement for the employers. The keepers are basically punishing people for not working and not generating the revenue that the prison has promised the outside contractors they would get. So you can see, also, there's a lot of room for corruption and abuse just by the very way that this whole kind of system is organized.

DAVIES: You know, one theme that runs throughout this documentary series from the earliest times of the republic to today is racism and its connection to law enforcement. NOVICK: Henry Smith was a teenager in the town of Paris, Texas, and he was accused of killing and possibly molesting a little girl - a 4-year-old girl. And during the time of this man hunt for him, it really became a frenzy. So by the time he was captured and brought back to the town, I think the whole nation was watching. And there were thousands of people that came there from all over the state of Texas, especially chartered trains were brought in to watch him be put to death in the most horrific, barbaric way you can imagine.

DAVIES: Now, was Henry Smith mentally handicapped in some way?

NOVICK: He was known in the town to be weak minded or feeble minded. That could be that he had an intellectual disability or a mental illness or both. And he was known for erratic behavior. But there was no due process here, so he was killed in front of thousands of people and tortured without ever having a chance to talk to a lawyer, have a trial, have representation or have any kind of legal system functioning to see whether anything that he was accused of actually happened.

DAVIES: Right. It was said that a crowd of 10,000 made their way to Paris, Texas, who witnessed this. As you said, trains were actually chartered to bring people there. DAVIES: That was in 1893, but, you know, as the documentary notes, this kind of unrestrained violence against African American continued, particularly in the South, well into the middle of the 20th century, and it's interesting that lynchings would often occur on a courthouse lawn to make the point that this was, in effect, you know, if not a legal act, one supported by a local establishment.

NOVICK: Yes, exactly, condoned, for sure, and often participated in by the sheriff, the district attorney and the leading citizens of the town or the city. Absolutely. That's correct. And it's - you know, this isn't really about crime and punishment and justice. This is about maintaining the social order and making sure that the caste system - the Jim Crow caste system stayed in place and that it would be done by fear.

You know, you're right about how police departments came to be. And it was really because cities grew with immigration in the 1830s, '40s and '50s and the anonymity of city life made crime easier. NOVICK: Yeah, New York City is the first city to create a police department. And then Boston and many other cities, Philadelphia. Pretty quickly, most major cities had police departments. And they were part of the patronage system, which meant that the political party in power gave out jobs to people that had supported them. And then those people often paid back sort of a kickback to whoever got them that job. So corruption was really built-in from the beginning of how police came to be. And, you know, we interviewed William Bratton, who was a commissioner of New York City Police Department and also LA and Boston. And he concurred that policing was extremely corrupt and extremely brutal in its origins.

And police often were asked to not just patrol the streets but protect illegal businesses that were sort of morals businesses - gambling, brothels - businesses that were going to go on anyway, somehow. And so, instead of arresting everyone who was running a brothel or a gambling den or an opium den, or an illegal saloon, they would basically walk the beat, take a kickback and let the place stay open. And anyone who didn't pay them was made to pay or got beat up. And all of this was revealed in a pretty explosive investigation of New York City policing that happened in the 1890s. And George Appo, who we were speaking about earlier, he was a star witness at that hearing or that investigation. And he talked a lot about the police corruption and brutality that was built-in.

DAVIES: Right. And there are waves of reform. There were scandals. You know, people were driven out of office who tolerated the stuff, but somehow, eventually, they found their way back. NOVICK: Vollmer, yeah.

DAVIES: Who took a different approach. Tell us about him.

NOVICK: Yeah, so he was a true progressive era reformer. You know, really believed that government could do good for people and make the society better and lift people up, and that police forces could be part of that. And he tried to professionalize his department in Berkeley. And his ideas about policing spread around the country.

And so he's actually known as the father of modern policing. And he created a college curriculum and sort of a training academy - that didn't exist before - and, I think, criteria for advancement that were grounded in knowledge and experience and not just who you knew and who you paid off. And he wanted his officers to see themselves as there to help people, not necessarily to arrest everybody or to take revenge if people didn't obey their commands, that kind of thing. In some ways, a lot of his advances helped policing to become more professional, less brutal, and less corrupt.

DAVIES: You know, prohibition comes in the early 20th century. It was supposed to make society more sober and less violent. And is this where organized crime got its start in urban America?

NOVICK: Yes. So there were always criminal gangs, but they were very local. And what happened with prohibition was that there was a much bigger incentive to get organized nationally and to form, basically, a system so that if you're bringing alcohol from one area to another, you're not going to have to fight your way there. And so, some of the smartest people involved in illicit activity, gangsters and mobsters in the '20s, formed a national crime syndicate. That's Lucky Luciano, Meyer Lansky and many other people that really sort of understood that the best thing for us to do here is to organize ourselves and keep a low profile.

They didn't want to have battles in the streets. They wanted to just figure out, OK, you stay in your territory, I'll stay in my territory. And if we have to move things, we'll work it out so that we don't, you know, run into each other unexpectedly. And that became basically the origin story for organized crime in America.

DAVIES: Yeah. And some of those families would endure for decades. Now, this was also a period when J. Edgar Hoover emerged as an important figure in law enforcement.
